sources.title: Group Theory: Application to the Physics of Condensed Matter
sources.referenceNote: The user-provided 2008_Book_GroupTheory.pdf has 576 physical pages. PDF page numbers below start at 1 and were checked against chapter headers. Lessons are original Chinese explanations without scanned book pages. The bibliographic DOI uses the publisher-verified ending 5.

sources.title: Crystallographic shelves: space-group hierarchy explained
sources.referenceNote: Primary teaching references on crystal systems, Bravais types,  space group  types, and enantiomorphic classification.

sources.title: How to read (and understand) Volume A of International Tables for Crystallography: an introduction for nonspecialists
sources.referenceNote: Teaching notes on space-group tables, general and special positions, and unit-cell settings.

sources.title: Double crystallographic groups and their representations on the Bilbao Crystallographic Server
sources.referenceNote: Original paper on Bilbao double-group definitions, SU(2) lifts, standard settings, and representation labeling.

sources.title: Magnetic Group Tables
sources.referenceNote: Classification totals and standardized tables for  magnetic point group  and  magnetic space group .

sources.title: Tutorial on the magnetic section of the Bilbao Crystallographic Server
sources.referenceNote: Official tutorials on MGENPOS, BNS/OG settings and symmetry operations of magnetic structures.

sources.title: Magnetic Space Groups: Bilbao teaching lecture
sources.referenceNote: Group structures of the four magnetic-space-group types and their classification counts 230, 230, 674, 517.

sources.title: Teaching crystallographic and magnetic point group symmetry using three-dimensional rendered visualizations
sources.referenceNote: Teaching material on polar vectors, axial vectors, primed operations, and  magnetic point group .

sources.title: Antiferromagnetic topological insulators
sources.referenceNote: Original research on combined time-reversal and half-translation symmetry; this course uses it to explain symmetry algebra and does not infer a topological phase directly from magnetic-group type.

sources.title: MSGCorep: corepresentations of magnetic space groups
sources.referenceNote: Upstream project for this workbench's magnetic-group data and corepresentation interfaces. Standard labels are displayed separately from temporary numerical site indices.

sources.title: AFLOW：Rock Salt/Halite (NaCl, B1) Structure
sources.note: Official prototype library: verify Fm-3m, fcc translations, and two site sets differing by (1/2,1/2,1/2). The model places Na at the origin; a  origin choice  exchanging chemical motifs does not change the  space group  type.

sources.title: AFLOW：Diamond (A4) Structure
sources.note: Official prototype library checking the diamond structure, Si isotypes and No.227. This page uses origin choice 2; the lesson shifts the origin to a Si atom and uses the common basis 0 and (1/4,1/4,1/4).

sources.title: AFLOW：Zincblende (B3) Structure
sources.note: Official prototype library, verifying No.216 and tetrahedral coordination of two atom types. The GaAs model selects Ga at 4a and As at 4c.

sources.title: AFLOW：Body-Centered Cubic (A2, bcc) Structure
sources.note: Official prototype library: verify bcc nuclear positions and No.229; this teaching model specifies the  ferromagnetic  direction separately.

sources.title: AFLOW：Rutile (TiO2, C4) Structure
sources.note: Official rutile prototype, checking the 2a/4f fractional coordinates of No.136; used for the chemical structure type of MnF2.

sources.title: Stout & Reed (1954)：The Crystal Structure of MnF2, FeF2, CoF2, NiF2 and ZnF2
sources.note: Original X-ray structural study: MnF2 is rutile at 25°C with a=4.8734 Å, c=3.3099 Å, u=0.310(3). The lesson uses rounded c/a=0.68 and u=0.310, not a low-temperature refinement.

sources.title: Yamani, Tun & Ryan (2010)：Neutron scattering study of the classical antiferromagnet MnF2
sources.note: Original neutron-scattering teaching experiment supporting antiparallel c-axis moments on the two rutile Mn sublattices. Ligand moments and finite-temperature fluctuations neglected here are not claimed to be strict experimental zeros.

sources.title: Roth (1958)：Magnetic Structures of MnO, FeO, CoO, and NiO
sources.note: Original neutron-diffraction study supporting antiferromagnetically stacked (111) ferromagnetic planes and in-plane moments in NiO.

sources.title: Pomjakushin (2024)：On the magnetic and crystal structures of NiO and MnO
sources.note: Original diffraction study discussing low-temperature lattice distortion and discrimination of magnetic-structure models. An ideal cubic parent phase or a few operations cannot replace experimental magnetic-group refinement.

sources.title: Weber et al. (2024)：Surface Magnetization in Antiferromagnets: Classification, Example Materials, and Relation to Magnetoelectric Responses
sources.note: The NiO case uses (111) layers and in-plane [11-2] moments, selecting one ideal magnetic domain for the lesson.

sources.title: Color groups arising from index-n subgroups of symmetry groups
sources.referenceNote: Acta Cryst. A71, 216–224; original research on color symmetry and color-preserving subgroups. This course uses original finite-permutation and three-layer periodic exercises.

sources.title: Colored lattices
sources.referenceNote: PNAS 75, 5264–5267; the original paper on three-dimensional colored lattices and color permutations.

sources.title: Algorithm for spin symmetry operation search
sources.referenceNote: Acta Cryst. A80, 94–103; spin-space operations, structural matching, and identifying the spin-only stabilizer from the span of magnetic moments.

sources.title: Crystal tensor properties of magnetic materials with and without spin–orbit coupling. Application of spin point groups as approximate symmetries
sources.referenceNote: Acta Cryst. A81, 317–338;  spin point group , independent spin/spatial transformations, and magnetic subgroups locked by SOC.

sources.title: Enumeration of Spin-Space Groups: Toward a Complete Description of Symmetries of Magnetic Orders
sources.referenceNote: Phys. Rev. X14, 031039; explains classification assumptions, periodicity indices and the range of infinite types. This site supplies teaching models and does not claim to enumerate all spin space groups.

scope: Original Chinese pedagogical lessons with cited sources
Ordinary single/double-valued workbench links for all 230 space groups
Magnetic catalog preserves the 1651 MSG and 122 MPG identifiers from the frozen upstream database
Seven Python demonstration families with explicit coordinate, phase and physical applicability conventions
Reference textbook PDF and page images not redistributed
Six material case studies with explicit parent phases and selected ideal magnetic domains
Interactive 3D camera rendering Python-calculated structures and axial moments
Guided derivations with individually revealed steps and separate mastery progress
Double, color and spin group teaching at point-group and three-dimensional space-group levels
Independent spin and lattice operations, spin-only stabilizers and SOC-locked magnetic subgroup explained
Finite motifs and periodic generators are verified; no arbitrary color/spin-space classification claimed
